title: Insurance Pitfalls in Fort Worth, Texas: Navigating Your Coverage
metaDescription: Discover common insurance pitfalls in Fort Worth, TX, and learn how to navigate your coverage effectively after a car accident.
excerpt: Educational Fort Worth, TX guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Confirm coverage at the scene
paragraphs: Ask for insurance card photos and verify policy status. In Fort Worth, uninsured motorist rates track with statewide averages — always assume minimum limits until verified.

sections.heading: Your UM/UIM policy in Texas
paragraphs: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage on your policy may pay when the at-fault driver has no coverage or insufficient 30/60/25 limits.
Notify your carrier promptly; UM claims still require documentation of injuries and damages.

sections.heading: Hit-and-run steps in Fort Worth
paragraphs: Report hit-and-runs immediately to Fort Worth police. UM coverage often requires a police report within 24–72 hours.
Seek witnesses and camera footage near Fort Worth downtown interchange.

sections.heading: Medical and financial documentation
paragraphs: Use Fort Worth Regional Medical Center if injured. Track lost wages and transportation costs.

sections.heading: When litigation may be necessary
paragraphs: If UM/UIM carriers deny or lowball offers, a licensed Texas attorney can evaluate bad-faith and negligence claims against the at-fault driver directly.

sections.heading: Fort Worth medical resources after a crash
paragraphs: Fort Worth residents often use Fort Worth Regional Medical Center, Fort Worth General Hospital after serious collisions. Level I trauma care is available at Fort Worth Level I Trauma Center.
Document every provider visit — gaps in treatment are a common reason TX insurers reduce settlement offers.
Keep receipts for prescriptions, imaging (MRI/CT), physical therapy, and medical transport.
list: Photograph visible injuries the same day when safe
Follow discharge instructions and keep all after-visit summaries
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for the adjuster

sections.heading: Local crash patterns: I-95, I-75
paragraphs: The metro area sees roughly 26,237 reported crashes annually (est.). High-risk areas include Fort Worth downtown interchange; Major highway corridor near Fort Worth.
If your collision occurred near I-95, note mile markers, exit numbers, and direction of travel for the police report.
Texas DOT data is available via https://www.txdot.gov/ — useful when disputing fault or road conditions.

sections.heading: Fort Worth County reports, courts, and evidence
paragraphs: Request the official crash report through the investigating agency. Fort Worth County Civil Court handles many civil injury filings in the region.
Business security video near Fort Worth retail corridors is often deleted within 7–30 days — send preservation letters quickly when appropriate.
The Fort Worth Bar Association offers lawyer-referral resources; WreckMatch LLC can also connect you with independent Texas attorneys at no obligation.

sections.heading: Educational disclaimer
paragraphs: WreckMatch LLC is a legal referral service — not a law firm. This Fort Worth guide is general education only and does not create an attorney-client relationship.
Laws and insurance rules change; verify all deadlines, coverage, and rights with a licensed Texas attorney before making decisions about your claim.

sections.heading: Settlement timeline expectations in Fort Worth
paragraphs: Minor property-damage claims in Fort Worth may resolve in weeks, but injury claims involving treatment, lost wages, or disputed fault often take months. Insurers may request recorded statements, independent medical exams, and broad medical authorizations — review each request carefully.
Texas uses 51% bar comparative negligence with a 2-year statute of limitations for most injury cases. Calendar your deadline from the date of injury.

If you were transported from I-95 to Fort Worth Regional Medical Center, keep ambulance, ER, and follow-up bills organized. UM/UIM and MedPay endorsements may apply when the other driver is underinsured.
list: Do not accept the first settlement check if treatment is ongoing
Avoid discussing fault on social media
Request adjuster denials or reservations of rights in writing
Compare repair estimates with your insurer's appraisal
Consult a licensed attorney before signing general releases

sections.heading: Document checklist for Fort Worth claims
paragraphs: Organize a folder (physical or digital) for every document tied to your Fort Worth crash: police report number, insurance claim numbers, tow and storage receipts, and rental car agreements.
Request itemized medical bills from Fort Worth Regional Medical Center rather than summary statements — itemized bills help catch billing errors and support future negotiations.
list: Photos of all vehicles and the scene from multiple angles
Employer note for any missed work shifts
Insurance adjuster name, phone, and claim number
Repair estimates from at least two body shops

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Fort Worth case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Texas?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 2-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.

faq.question: Will my rates increase if I use UM/UIM coverage?
faq.answer: Rules vary by carrier and state. Ask your insurer in writing; using UM after a not-at-fault crash is often protected — verify your policy.

faq.question: Where can I get a crash report in Fort Worth?
faq.answer: Contact the investigating agency listed on your exchange-of-information form. Fort Worth County reports may also be available through local police or https://www.txdot.gov/.
